questions.question: Which dinosaur is this?
questions.explanation: A copy of a Diplodocus skeleton, nicknamed Dippy, greeted visitors to London's Natural History Museum for decades.

questions.question: Which dinosaur is this?
questions.explanation: The biggest T. rex tooth ever found was about 30 cm long, roots and all, longer than a banana.

media.alt: A huge dinosaur skeleton standing on two legs

questions.question: Which of these animals was already around at the time of the dinosaurs?
questions.explanation: Sharks were swimming in the seas long before the first dinosaurs appeared, and they are still here today.

questions.question: Which dinosaur had two rows of big plates along its back and spikes on its tail?
questions.explanation: Stegosaurus lived around 150 million years ago, about 80 million years before T. rex.

questions.question: What do we call a scientist who studies fossils?
questions.explanation: Palaeontologists study ancient life, while archaeologists study the things people left behind.

questions.question: Which dinosaur's name means 'swift thief'?
questions.explanation: Real Velociraptors were about the size of a turkey and covered in feathers.

questions.question: What did long-necked dinosaurs like Brachiosaurus eat?
questions.explanation: Their long necks let them reach leaves high up in the treetops.

questions.question: Roughly when did the last of the giant dinosaurs die out?
questions.explanation: A huge asteroid crashed into the Earth at about that time, and most scientists think that is what wiped them out.

questions.question: Which animals alive today are descended from dinosaurs?
questions.explanation: Birds are living dinosaurs, so a robin on your bird table is a distant cousin of T. rex.

questions.question: Which of these prehistoric reptiles could fly?
questions.explanation: Pteranodon soared over the seas at the time of the dinosaurs, but it was a pterosaur, not a dinosaur.

questions.question: Which dinosaur had a heavy bony club on the end of its tail?
questions.explanation: Ankylosaurus was covered in bony armour, like a living tank.

questions.question: Which young fossil hunter found amazing fossils on the beach at Lyme Regis in the early 1800s?
questions.explanation: Mary Anning was only about 12 when she helped dig up the skeleton of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea reptile.

questions.question: Which dinosaur had a long, hollow crest on its head that it may have used to make honking calls?
questions.explanation: Air passing through the tubes inside its crest may have made a deep, trumpeting sound.

questions.question: In which country were the bones of the first dinosaur ever given a scientific name found?
questions.explanation: Megalosaurus, named in 1824 from bones found in Oxfordshire, was the first dinosaur ever given a scientific name.

questions.question: Which prehistoric animal is this famous fossil?
questions.explanation: The first Archaeopteryx skeletons were found in Germany in the 1860s and 1870s, with feathered wings but also teeth and a long bony tail.

questions.question: Which dinosaur is this?
questions.explanation: Unlike most long-necked dinosaurs, Brachiosaurus had front legs longer than its back legs, a bit like a giraffe.

questions.question: Which dinosaur is this?
questions.explanation: Early reconstructions put Iguanodon's spiky thumb on its nose, mistaking it for a horn.

media.alt: A tall dinosaur skeleton in a museum hall

questions.question: In which geological period did Tyrannosaurus rex live?
questions.explanation: Despite the film title, T. rex lived in the Late Cretaceous, more than 70 million years after the Jurassic ended.

questions.question: Which was the earliest of the three periods of the age of dinosaurs?
questions.explanation: The first dinosaurs appeared in the Triassic, followed by the Jurassic and then the Cretaceous.

questions.question: Which scientist coined the word 'dinosaur'?
questions.explanation: Richard Owen came up with the name in the early 1840s, and later campaigned for London's Natural History Museum.

questions.question: What is thought to have made Spinosaurus unusual among giant meat-eating dinosaurs?
questions.explanation: Spinosaurus had a long, crocodile-like snout and probably spent much of its time hunting in rivers.

questions.question: The Chicxulub crater, left by the asteroid linked to the dinosaurs' extinction, is in which country?
questions.explanation: The crater, more than 150 km wide, lies buried under the Yucatan Peninsula and the sea beside it.

questions.question: What is the name for a fossilised dinosaur dropping?
questions.explanation: Coprolites can reveal what a dinosaur ate, right down to crushed bones and bits of plant.

questions.question: What are the gastroliths found with some dinosaur skeletons?
questions.explanation: Some plant-eating dinosaurs swallowed stones, which may have helped grind up food in their stomachs.

questions.question: Which dinosaur's name means 'tyrant lizard king'?
questions.explanation: Rex is Latin for king, and T. rex is one of the very few dinosaurs that most people know by its full scientific name.

questions.question: Giganotosaurus, one of the largest meat-eating dinosaurs ever found, was discovered in which country?
questions.explanation: It was found in Patagonia in 1993, and its name means 'giant southern lizard'.

questions.question: Which dinosaur had a thick, bony dome on top of its head?
questions.explanation: Its name means 'thick-headed lizard', and its dome of bone could be more than 20 cm thick.

questions.question: Which island is often called the dinosaur capital of Britain?
questions.explanation: Dinosaur bones and footprints still wash out of the Isle of Wight's crumbling cliffs after winter storms.

questions.question: Roughly how long ago did the first dinosaurs appear?
questions.explanation: Dinosaurs then lived on Earth for more than 160 million years before the giant ones died out.
